steps.text: The 'Saint' drags her massive body along as she walks at the head of the procession. The Sankta named Lemuel jumps around, pulling out gun after gun like prestidigitation, raining a hail of gunfire onto her quarry.
But the 'Saint' barely even spares her a glance.
Her halo shimmers, and despite the great distance separating them, Patrizion still hears her 'voice' with perfect clarity.
Their empathy is growing stronger, which means their long journey approaches its end.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Allow our other cohorts to take care of your friend's remains, Patrizion. We do not need to mourn him.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Your Beatitude...

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Do you still remember that arborbeast fledgling?

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: If we reach our destination, Laterano shall recreate the miracle of life once more. Every miracle, freely performed.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: You mean...?

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: And so, we move onwards.
The grand procession passes statues after statue, workshop after workshop. The city grows brighter, step by step, pace by pace.
Patrizion walks forward in silence.
S... Stop.
A young gunsmith's apprentice walks against the flow of people, stopping in front of Patrizion. Vannini stares down the gun-knight, many times taller than her. She raises her gun against him.
The crowd parts around them, but none look toward them. Vannini bites her lip, doing her best to stop her hand from trembling.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Ah, you are his apprentice, yes?

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Magister Paganini... Where is he?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: He...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: He warned me. So in the dream, I-I... hid in the workshop. After I awoke, I still hesitated for so long...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Right now, you're... scary. Laterano's scary. I don't know what's going on, I don't even have a patron firearm...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: But I can't just hide and wait...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: So you made yourself that gun and came to stop me?

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: That's very brave of you.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: But do you see this procession, my child? We will birth a miracle, one that nearly all Laterans will be a part of.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: It's not 'scary'.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: (Shakes head) That's got... nothing to do with me.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: I'm not very... good with words. I couldn't... couldn't think of any worse ones...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Magister Paganini was... my only family...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: My only... connection... to Laterano...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Your only connection, huh...?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Pag, you never got a halo in the dream, so why did you join the procession?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: To find a chance to kill you, obviously.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: That sniper, your old student?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Tragic, isn't it?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Worse than when Gia left?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: You still going to listen to that monster? Going to keep protecting the crowd on this walk?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Don't think I don't know what you're thinking.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: The Laterano of fifty years ago forced you to banish an infected Liberi. The Laterano of ten years ago forced you to banish a fallen gun-knight.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Even your granddaughter is far too stubborn and opinionated. Who knows if someday, she too will...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: So, you hope for a better Laterano?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: You want it to be like a doctor who becomes a miracle worker, able to treat Oripathy, able to fix personality flaws, able to make everyone accept one another, no questions asked?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: That way, no more sad farewells like you've suffered through before?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: *cough*... You're a coward through and through, Patrizion!

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Farewells are like melted ice cream and worn-out guns. Doesn't matter what you do, it's bound to happen, right?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Even if you can't stop them from happening, you can still give your well-wishes. A simple 'goodbye' is all you need.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: It's not like you have a speech impediment like Vannini. Is it so hard to find a way to shed some of your regret?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Enough talk! Just hang on!

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Hang on, my feathery ass—*cough*—This is... a bullet that can cut right through gun-knight armor...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Don't touch me. Let me finish, otherwise I'll step into the grave that much quicker.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: A-Alright then...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: What's with the tone? Don't even think about getting sentimental on me, Patrizion!

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Why do you think I saved you?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Don't jabber at me about calamity or crisis or what path Laterano should take...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: If the city really is going to be destroyed, surely we can do more than just leave it to some monster from beyond our nightmares that sprang up out of nowhere?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Aurela, Fiammetta, all those other Laterans you know... Are these connections that weak to you?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: You're a gun-knight, you stulte! The best gun-knight in all of Laterano!

spans.text: The best gun-knight in all of Laterano!

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: *cough* *cough*—
Paganini gets more intense the more he rambles, but his voice grows quieter by the second.
Patrizion holds his old friend tight, feeling the warmth slowly drain out of him, as though the last dregs of his life had spilled out with his latest outburst.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Hey, not going to say anything?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Never mind then. Before, at the Shrine, I said we never actually shared anything these past few decades...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Now, at the very least... That regret's gone.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: My magister, he...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Forgive me. I couldn't even give you one final moment with Pag.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: *sob*—

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Vannini, i-if you had just... been a bit quicker... making this gun, if you had just gotten here quicker...
Vannini lowers her head as if in a daze. She looks about at the people walking past, like she is only just noticing her surroundings.
Her halo suddenly begins to shine. All it would take is a momentary waver of the heart, and the empathy of the countless masses would come crashing down on this confused, lonely Sankta.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: No, child.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Keep a tight grip on your gun!

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Ggh...
For a moment, Patrizion feels pain, but it is followed by a gentle, yet irrefusable comfort. It flows from her, from those enlightened creatures, from his people in the procession.
He knows his unusual reaction has been noticed, prompting the crashing waves of empathy, like seawater forcing its way back upriver.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Ah—
Patrizion feels dizzy. He sighs, and slowly crouches down.
A moment later, the elderly gun-knight grips the barrel of the gunsmith's apprentice's gun, pointing it towards him.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Vannini. I got your name right, I hope?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Vannini, no matter how long it took you, or for what reason you did it, you made your very first patron firearm. That makes you a qualified gunsmith.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: But that is not enough. You must learn how to use it.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Now is a perfect opportunity.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Wh-What do you mean?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Keep it steady. Yes, just like that. Calm your mind, then, pull the trigger.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: You... You didn't kill Magister Paganini. Also, I'll fa... fall—

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I am responsible for what happened to Pag, but this is not to avenge him.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: At this very moment, Laterano is walking down a new path. Faith flows into faith, and new prayers congregate into a collective consensus.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: You are too close to the procession. Empathy will soon swallow you whole. Only by falling can you break away.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Once you have fallen, I'll go guide the others. This is my duty, the duty of a gun-knight.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: I don't understand. Why... do you do this?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I don't really know myself, haha. I'm an old addlepate, after all.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I always believed that, were Paradise to become a true paradise, our connections would become unbreakable.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: But what if in the course of all that, we lost more than we already had?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: We might ease our regrets, but when the time comes, what if our success has lost all meaning?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: If we were once all devils, if we once carried our sins together, how could our connections ever be broken?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: O glorious Sankta, O favored of faith, what have you to fear?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: (Pained inhalation)

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Vannini, girl, fear not falling into hell.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: This is the first lesson you should learn... and I'm right with you.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: It just never ends...

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: If this keeps on, I'm gonna have to start smacking them with my weapon!

steps.name: Sankta Errari
steps.text: Me too.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: My hand's getting numb, can barely hold my staff.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Don't know how it's going on Fiammetta's side of things. According to the plan, once she sets the explosives, we'll blow up the plate's locking mechanisms and send all of Pagus Saint Marcel adrift.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: It'll also cut those monsters off from the Basilica.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Tsch. If we can hold on that long.

spans.text: we can hold on that long.

steps.text: Dispersing Arrows!
Leave them to me!

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: These clothes...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Landen Guard temporary solo combat team, Hildegard, at your service!

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Landen... Sorry, never heard of you.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: It's fine, I'm used to it, haha.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Some of my Sankta sisters are in that procession. We were running our business when we got called back, and then... we went through a whole bunch of stuff.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: How should I put this...? Even if everything that happened was fake, and Landen Monastery hasn't actually been given important responsibilities by the Curia...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: As long as I'm here, Laterano will once again remember the name of Landen Monastery!

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: These monsters might look strange, but they're hardly more of a challenge than the beasts of the great snowcapped mountains.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I've got enough arrows, and I've got a sharp eye. I'll help you hold them off!

steps.name: Sankta Errari
steps.text: But we're all tired out, kid. We've racked our brains and put in the effort, but all we can do is keep falling back.

steps.name: Sankta Errari
steps.text: We're not exactly settling any grudges here. We came back to Laterano just to suffer again.

steps.name: Fallen Angel
steps.text: It's almost time, Mostima. Still no news from that Lemuen lady?

steps.name: Fallen Angel
steps.text: If we can't disengage the defenses on the plate lock mechanism, we won't be able to blow through their armor plating, right?

steps.name: Sankta Errari
steps.text: Let's just call it here then.

steps.name: Sankta Errari
steps.text: If those guys reach the Basilica, then what happens? Everyone more or less becomes Sankta?

steps.name: Sankta Errari
steps.text: What's that got to do with us?

steps.name: Sankta Errari
steps.text: Look around you. We can't even cobble together a single halo. Our long-awaited reinforcements are just one Liberi nun.

steps.name: Sankta Errari
steps.text: We've got an entire city's worth of people against us. Why do we Alieni have to hold all of them off?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Come now, that's not the best attitude to have right now...

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Because right now, we're the only ones who can.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: We're always having to bust our asses doing things ordinary Sankta take for granted, right?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I had a little accident, as you can see. If I hadn't become a Legatus, I don't know what I'd be doing right now.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I said I was going to be doing Messenger stuff when I left the Holy City, but I was just wandering around, really.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Wandering to places without any Sankta, places where these black horns on my head don't stand out, places where silent empathy's the norm...

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: It was hard.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: It took two whole years before I could look my friends in the eyes again without breaking out in a sweat.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Liberi, Fallen Angels, we're obsessed with assimilating or getting our old lives back. After putting in all that effort, why go with the hatchet job?
Well, how about that.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I never thought I'd hear those words coming out of your mouth, Mostima.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Promise me you'll forget you heard anything.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Forget what?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: How did things go on your end?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Good news is, the bombs are in place.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Bad news is, I was afraid they wouldn't be enough to blow through all the lock mechanisms, so I shoved the rest of my grenades in there with them...

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Which means I'm all out of grenades to shoot at these things.

steps.name: Enlightened Creature A
steps.text: (Halo rapidly flickers)

steps.name: Enlightened Creature B
steps.text: (Continuous sounds of prayer)

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Hey, Fiammetta, let's blow this joint.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Wait! We still haven't heard anything from Lemuen. If the defenses aren't disengaged in time, all our explosives will go to waste!

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Time to explosion, one minute!

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Wha-?
The timer starts ticking down in Fiammetta's hand. The enlightened creatures stop their prayers. As if sensing something is up, they throw themselves at her like rabid beasts.
Hildegard reaches for her quiver. It's empty.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Fifty seconds!
Sorry, everyone! Hope I'm not too late!

A wheelchair suddenly brakes, throwing up a cloud of dust as it screeches across the ground. Its rider spins its left wheel as she hoists her rifle with her right hand, her long hair fluttering in the air.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: You're right on time!

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Good to know we're still in sync!

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The two of you will never guess how hard I beat my old wheelchair speed-shooting record by after I broke through their cordon around the Seventh Tribunal!

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Forty seconds!

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I heard what you said just now. Fallen Angels, Liberi, Alieni... I'm inclined to use another term to sum up our relationship.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Friends, countrymen—Laterans!

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I've solved the permissions issue. The lock mechanism defenses are disengaged. Everyone, retreat to the Basilica doors! I'll hold these monsters off.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Thirty seconds!

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: You're going to shoot them, Lemuen? You'll fall!

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I hate to admit it, but I can sense what you're thinking.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: So shut those mouths of yours. Laterano doesn't need to be saved! By you! Like this!
The click of bullets loading and the thrumming of the monsters' hearts reverberate through Lemuen's ears. She is nearly face-to-face with them, going against every sniper's instinct she has.
She listens to her own breathing, calm and steady.
Under these conditions, how fast can a sniper fire? Time to find out.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Lemuen, Cardinal of the Seventh Tribunal. In the name of Laterano's national security, I sentence you to death!

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: No matter the cost!

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Five seconds.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It's done.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Lemuen, your halo... You alright? Feel anything weird?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Ngh—
A violent explosion tears through every inch of the ground in front of the Basilica, a rift plowing itself through the plaza.
On the other side of the rift, the grand procession shows itself as it marches forward.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Is that... El?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Hey, turns out it was my sis and her crew! They did a real bang-up job!

steps.name: Enlightened Creature A
steps.text: (Wounded wail)

steps.name: Enlightened Creature B
steps.text: (Fragmented prayer)

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Retreat somewhere safe, for the time being.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: A rift... One my people cannot cross. But we once forded raging rivers and traversed great valleys. Compared to those dangers, this is nothing.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: He lies ahead. I shall not stop.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: *cough* I... I never said I'd let you pass.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Your body is weak. I fear you have not an ounce of strength left. Am I wrong?
Exusiai does not answer.
She has told herself the entire time to ignore how tired she feels, how strange falling makes her feel. She continues her barrage against the saint's colossal body, but once again to no avail.

The saint makes no move against her. Rather, she continues to cradle her, the same way she did when they left the dream. Never before has such a strange cradle been seen, one made from a malformed yet mighty arm.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Even though you know the entire truth of both past and present, even though you know we are working to create a new miracle, like the birth of Laterano...

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Even though you know our journey thus far has been to awaken our Lord, to ensure that in the future with but a hair's breadth separating destruction from continuation, the Sankta shall persist...

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Why do you still stand against us?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Am I the only one?

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: With empathy that strong, I don't believe for a second you can't feel it!

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: After so many long years of waiting, I finally got my chance, but... it was all just a dream...

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: A dream's fine, too.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: If it's all a dream, then I don't have to worry about anything. Maybe getting shot here doesn't mean anything in reality!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: If this is a dream, then I shall wake. If this is obsession, then I shall shatter it.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Let us only speak of redemption after that.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Vannini, girl, fear not falling into hell.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: This is the first lesson you should learn... and I'm right with you.

steps.name: Fearful Child
steps.text: East of the east of La Unidad♪ Laterano, holy city of white♪

steps.name: Panicking Child
steps.text: There, the earth hides no bombs♪ There, the fields share wheat most bright♪

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: All shall bask in His love♪

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I hate to admit it, but I can sense what you're thinking.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: So shut those mouths of yours. Laterano doesn't need to be saved! By you! Like this!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I'm just an ordinary Lateran. Nobody important, and I don't have any special skills.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: So when I listened to you talk about the origins of the Sankta, the history of Laterano, the essence of faith, the crazy truth behind the life we're used to...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I was shocked! Shocked right down to my core!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: If things really are like you say, then the life we enjoyed in Laterano really is a kind of miracle.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: But since I'm just an ordinary Lateran, while you were explaining everything happening around us, all I noticed was...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: How nobody looked happy at all.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Shouldn't Laterano be a happy place?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: If... If lots of our people will suffer when we complete this journey, how am I supposed to believe you can make the miracle happen?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Wait, no, scratch that, how am I supposed to believe it's a miracle in the first place?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: So, even if I wasn't around, there'd be other Sankta to stand against you.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: I shared all I have seen and all I have experienced, yet you still choose to turn away?

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: The path of the Sankta is a cruel one, our faith paved with sin and suffering.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Have their years inside this peculiar, distorted Paradise left our brethren so weak?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Ugh, you're not getting me at all.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Maybe I should be asking what you asked me earlier—

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Why you?

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: I have already told you my answer.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Even if this Terra-destroying calamity is real, and millions of Sankta are doomed, and Laterano's about to be completely screwed...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Why are you, a 'Saint', the only one who can bring us salvation?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: We're the ones who live in this city right now, who enjoy its blessings, who went through its changes, and who protected it from destruction.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: You don't exist anymore. You're just a ghost! A string of code I can shoot!

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Incorrect, my child. When I lifted my spear against my dying companion, the sleeping silver mounts answered me, and recorded my prayer for all eternity.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: All that is happening here and now is a continuation of that prayer.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Death cannot be undone, yet I wandered amongst His datastream. Together, we heard your prayers.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: No matter how appearances may change, no matter how the faith develops as time flows by, so long as the Sankta still pray, He shall operate eternally, and I shall forever be there...

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: The spiritual light will always shine on Laterano.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: This is our mission.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: ...Prayer is useless.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Pardon?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: To be honest, I learned a long time ago that prayer is useless.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: When I was in my third year of primary school, an investigator from the Sixth Tribunal did an experiment at our school.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: She said there were two groups of patients at Faber Central Hospital with more or less the same conditions, and split us into our own two groups. One group would pray every day, while the other didn't have to do anything.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: But in the end, there wasn't any difference in their recovery. The investigator told us the results in class: prayer is useless.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Haha, it's funny, really. This country's full of churches, but it's always doing these kinds of 'outrageous' experiments.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: (Halo flickers)

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: You're right, Laterans really do pray to the Lord every day.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Praying they'll get better soon after getting sick, praying they'll pick the coolest guardian gun ever, praying the caravans won't run into Catastrophes on the way home, praying they'll never have to say goodbye to their friends...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Praying that they'll be able to make it through all sorts of pain and suffering.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: But I never actually expected there to be a 'Lord' who would grant everyone's wishes, who would swoop in to save us when we're in trouble.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Empathy lets us sense the emotions of our people. It lets me know if the ones by my side are happy or sad.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: But prayer? Prayer doesn't just need me to sense things, it needs me to want to help my family and friends, to understand things outside of empathy.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: It even lets me feel like I could help some complete strangers get well sooner.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Even though I know it probably won't change a thing.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I met lots of Sankta while running around with Penguin Logistics. You'd be hard pressed to call some of them Father, while others don't live life like we do in the Holy City anymore.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: But they were all so... fulfilled. I still felt close to them.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I believe it's because we still prayed like we always did.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: It needs us to not doubt. It needs us to hold hope in our hearts.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Just being down to pray for each other is a beautiful thing in itself.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: It gives me a true connection to people.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: (Thunderous sigh)

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: If these connections were the foundation of faith, it would be exceedingly frail.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: No. I think it's exactly these connections that help hold our lives up.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: 'Survival'... 'Life'...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: If you don't understand why Sankta these days are all about desserts and explosions—

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: What's up with you?

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: (Fretful pacing)

The saint suddenly becomes exceptionally restless. She feels out the edge of the rift as she paces along it, her sharp front claws piercing the exposed, bent foundations, trying to find a way to climb down.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: This rift you have opened allows me to sense His signal much more clearly.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: He is below the Basilica, calling out for me to approach—

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: No, no... Why is His signal in such disarray... He is anxious, uneasy...

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: The Creator has already revoked... or perhaps.... there are other threats forcing Him to... change...
The sound of machinery, faint yet clear, rises out from the depths of the rift below their feet.
The saint's unease becomes increasingly obvious. Half of her body has already entered the fault. Her claws clench, and Exusiai senses that she is in great pain.
Behind her, the procession stops, countless halos flickering over and over due to her worry, like a river of paralyzed stars.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: Child, talks of past and present are meaningless... You need only step towards... the future...

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: You do not understand this crisis. There are no new solutions for you to find. You must... survive...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I said it before, I'm not letting you pass.

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: How are you meant to stop... a ghost... a string of code...?

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: (Mournful roar)
The saint's voice becomes garbled. She has reverted to barely more than a beast, like the Teekaz who trudged through the mud all those years ago.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: If we weren't in this mess, we could've been pretty good friends. A ghost, a string of code, the very first Sankta... There's no cooler friend than that!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Ah, silly me! Can't believe I forgot to introduce myself!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Lemuel of St. Theodore's Comprehensive School, number one student in the 84th Intercity Net Security preparatory course! And I've got the school certs to prove it!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Every bullet I got you with was custom-made! They just needed some time to take effect!
Her patron firearm howls once more. The force of the barrage finally frees Exusiai from the saint's grasp.
She leaps high into the sky.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: We're not going to give up on life, obviously, but we're definitely not going to go with your plan.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: If refusing it means the halos connecting us will be cut off, then cut them off.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Because even if you do, we will never stop praying for each other.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: We'll still give thanks to the Lord for His existence, even if He isn't what we thought He was.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: O Lord, thank you for being there, for blessing us with bread and bullets, for being there for us during our trials and tribulations!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Thank you for spreading the light across Laterano all this time, giving everyone the chance for salvation!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Thank you for clearing the way for us!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Amen. There, prayer done.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Let's say bye-bye, the wildest way I know—

steps.name: 'Saint'
steps.text: (Roars)
Explosives fall like rain, linking together into a chain of blasts as they collide with the bullets embedded in the saint's body.
The saint howls, but not because of the explosions, not because of her flesh wounds, but because of the strange, dissonant sound caused by the 'ammunition' as it scrapes across her skin.
The sound of data being erased.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Divine judgment, traditional!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Rock n' gospel!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Barrage, sky-shattering!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Apple pie, with char siu!

a.text: Humanity does not exist. Variable referred to as 'humanity' is a byproduct of Originium.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Originium?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: A... sea, made of Originium?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It's like the sea back home. Calm, beautiful, but one nobody dares to set out on it.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Maybe, maybe not. This is familiar to you because... because the sea by your hometown is here. There's even a part of you here too.

spans.text: Maybe, maybe not. This is familiar to you because... because the sea by your hometown is here. There's even a part of

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: All things that are have been sealed here. A coffin for the world and everything upon it.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Like the crystals left behind by Oripathy patients after they die?

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: If that helps you understand it, then yes.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Amazing, isn't it? This was once the end of everything.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: We are born far too late, our lives far too short. We even unconsciously take some inconsequential mishaps, and turn them into the foundation of our very being.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Like how you blindly took a shattered memory and turned it into divine revelation.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: But no matter. The Law wishes to bestow upon you true revelation.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: He says: 'None can be saved.'

a.text: Originium to Originium, dust to dust.
Personnel with relevant privileges have provided PCS with new set of directives. Cognitive radiation amplifier at maximum output. Effective range: Terra.
Originium will connect to PCS after maintenance is complete.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The Law created the Sankta from the Teekaz, built the order of Laterano in untamed wilds, and even attempted to establish a Terra-wide religion spanning multiple civilizations.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: He has worked for millennia in service of humanity. Surely it was not simply to turn all of it into Originium?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Is that truly the Law's ultimate goal?

a.text: This is the goal of Originium, not the goal of 'the Law'.
Originium has been set as a prerequisite of 'the Law'.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If Originium is as you earlier described, able to assimilate everything, why is it a prerequisite to anything?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Surely it is more than the end of everything?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: How would the Law be able to operate inside a field of uniform Originium? What would be the meaning of a halo in that case?

a.text: As Originium is the end of all things, there is meaning in bestowing halos on everything.
Angels before Originium are merely angels.
Angels after Originium are the only method of existence that will retain meaning.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: 'None can be saved'?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: So not even Laterano as it is, a cramped Paradise, can be preserved?

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: It cannot be saved, nor preserved.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: 'Save everyone' has never been a tenable commandment.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: All things march towards death. The only way to 'save' them is to see them off.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Grant them a dream, a bearing to hold themselves to. Hide their blemishes, espouse their brilliance.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: By doing so, you allow them to gladly accept their final journey.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Like how you saved yourself.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Granting dreams to others as a placebo?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: No. I won't accept that.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: If I have truly, shamelessly clung onto a false dream, put myself through a crucible for more than ten years...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: If I have debased myself by inflicting unhealing wounds upon countless others for the sake of self-salvation...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Then all the more reason not to spread this shamelessness and debasement to others.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Even if you accepted it, you are unable to perform such an act.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Only the Law can bestow such salvation.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: You can't possibly mean...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Keph's plan... was to give everyone halos, all so they can be granted this 'salvation'?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But how would becoming Sankta help? Are Sankta beyond callousness, beyond cruelty, beyond... suffering?!

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: We shall not stop at becoming Sankta.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: We will all become true angels, Andoain Agathangelos.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: True... angels?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Aggy... Agathangelos? I don't like this name. It's too long and hard to read, and it doesn't sound like any of the other names here.

steps.name: Sickly Woman
steps.text: This is... my surname. Before your father left, he kept telling me he hoped I would give it to you.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But, Mamma...

steps.name: Sickly Woman
steps.text: I know it's strange and hard to read, Andoain.

steps.name: Sickly Woman
steps.text: If the other children knew you had this name, they might say hurtful things to you like 'there's that weird boy!'.

steps.name: Sickly Woman
steps.text: Once you head out further afield, bandits may think you're a rich foreigner, while the Inquisition might assume you're a zealot up to no good.

steps.name: Sickly Woman
steps.text: Which is why I hope you never share it with others. Stick with a simple name, like the other orphans here.

steps.name: Sickly Woman
steps.text: I hope you will keep it in the deepest recesses of your heart, a place where your happiness, anger, sorrow and joy cannot touch.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But I feel really sad right now... I don't know if there's anywhere in me that doesn't feel sad.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Is there really a place like that in my heart?

steps.name: Sickly Woman
steps.text: Of course, Andoain. Everyone has one.

steps.name: Sickly Woman
steps.text: I hope that, when you think of this name, you will be free from suffering, grief, frustration, and strife.

steps.name: Sickly Woman
steps.text: Forget the dying and the hungry by the road who claw at your ankles. Forget those in despair, whose minds were eaten away by the sea fog, and the flesh they chew on.

steps.name: Sickly Woman
steps.text: Forget the monster doll your father made, and my finscale soup. Forget the storybook you keep beneath your pillow, and the brush you found in the old chapel.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But I don't want to forget them!

steps.name: Sickly Woman
steps.text: ...It's just for a little while, alright?

steps.name: Sickly Woman
steps.text: I hope that, when you think of this name, you will find tranquility... the tranquility of emptiness.

steps.name: Sickly Woman
steps.text: One day, you will need this peace.

steps.name: Sickly Woman
steps.text: Promise me, Andoain.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But I still want to know what this name means.

steps.name: Sickly Woman
steps.text: 'Angel'. In Lateran, it means... 'Angel'.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Tranquility... Yes, a very apt descriptor.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Behold. Even as they come, they do so in silence.
The ocean of Originium is endless. Those who look upon it soon realize that every observation they make of it is without meaning.
When everything the eye can see is impossible to differentiate, where to start looking is similarly impossible to determine.
But now, above this great sea of uniformity, something shines.

It is as if the edge of the Originium sea has converged into a river that flows into the heavens. Countless fragments of Originium rise up from the surface of the sea, floating up into the distant, empty beyond in perfect formation.
The fragments are jagged and irregular. Some are as small as dust, others as immense as stars, but all, without exception, are crowned with a glimmer of light.
A glimmer shaped like a ring.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Halos...

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Beautiful, aren't they?

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: It's a pity that all the beauty and ugliness in the world is meaningless to angels.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Angels are neither beautiful nor ugly. They are neither high nor low, noble nor base, reverent nor blasphemous, adorant nor disdainful.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: They know neither meeting nor separation, happiness nor suffering.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Can they even be considered life?

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Does that matter? All the praise we heap upon life is nothing but egotistical admiration.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Observing their forms in an attempt to compare them to our definition of life is simply us trying to find resonance with them.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Then, are they the Law? Are they gods?

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: If there is no distinction between beauty and ugliness, high and low, noble and base, why would there be one for god and worshiper?

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Angels do not understand faith. They simply exist in the furthest reaches of the universe, taking on the most distinctive forms.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: It was our forebears who encountered them, shamelessly disturbing them as they did so. In their name, we created a forgery of a dialectic, of god and worshiper.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: If all our emotions, ideas and actions have nothing to do with angels...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: What does our future have to do with them?

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: It is because everything we are has nothing to do with angels that we should become them.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Now, this is only a possibility, but...

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: When the Creator descends, when everything is submerged into this ocean before us, a time of stasis, uniformity, and meaninglessness...

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: The Sankta within can take on the forms of angels and enjoy an eternal existence, where they shall shine forevermore.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: This is the final answer we shall submit to death.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: This is His gift to the people He has guarded for thousands of years, His final blessing and salvation.

a.text: We drift, just as we drift between past and future.
We flicker, just as we flicker between reality and the void.
Angels know not beginnings or ends. Angels know not increase or decrease. Angels know not life or death.
In an existence where nothing exists, we can only exist in the form of angels.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: So these are true angels?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Incomprehensible to the point where the Law cannot directly describe them, instead defining them by what they are not?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Immaterial to the point where taking the form of angels allows one to continue to exist after becoming Originium?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: This is the existence the Law has chosen once everything returns to Originium?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If this is the ultimate purpose of the Law, then as a saint and an executor, I should implement and enforce it.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Unless...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Unless the Law itself is a paradox.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I have one final question!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Explain to me how, if angels truly are as you say, without beginning or end, increase or decrease, life or death...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Then why do they—you—have such a strong desire to exist... to continue to exist?
As machines have inputs, so they have outputs.
The saints sought answers in the Law, and the Law granted them revelation.
The fleet asked the system for instructions, so the system issued commands.
The Lord, or rather, PCS, has never been as silent as it is now.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You are an artificial system, so you require people to operate you. This is true for both a 'command system' and the Law worshiped by the Holy City.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The ultimate purpose you were given was to break humanity free from their shackles and return their angelic nature.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: However, this purpose, does it stem from people, or from angels?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Why would the angels you described desire this? Their actions do not have purpose, assuming they can even perform actions other than 'drift' and 'flicker'.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But if this purpose comes from people, how will you turn them into angels?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Surely everything you have done was more than just—

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Nurturer, I shall now grant you salvation.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Guide your people to angelification. Guide yourself.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: Be free from suffering, grief, frustration, and strife. You will obtain tranquility, the tranquility of emptiness, as shall those you have helped and harmed alike.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: You need not live as an egotist, a villain, a traitor, or a fanatic. Nor do you need to die as one.
Andoain feels more tired than he has ever been before, as if an entire lifetime's worth of burdens have been pressed down onto his back at once.
The arborbeast was right. He really is like that Sarkaz drunkard, acutely aware this is the last chance he has.
If he wanted relief, this is the only way.
'Relief'. He only needs to hear the word's crisp syllables to feel joy, to want to fall to the ground and weep until he has spent all his strength, then fall further into a deep slumber.
But he uses that strength to instead open his clouded eyes.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I don't know what kind of answer His Holiness gave you, nor do I know what Mostima, Fiammetta, Lemuen or her little sister are thinking right now aboveground.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I don't know where Patia and our former fellows are headed, nor do I know whose bosom the children I tended in the Shrine of Nurtury have clutched.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I don't know if they want this salvation, this relief.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But if what you really care about is my answer as a 'suitable candidate'...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Then my answer is no.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I'm far too conceited. Even to this very moment, I still refuse to believe my arduous search for answers, decades in the making, was all for this simple relief.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I'm not only conceited, I'm an egotist, a villain, a traitor, and a fanatic. And so I suffer and grieve, my frustrations giving rise to strife.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But they are the foundations of my life.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: If I were to abandon them, the one who obtains relief, who becomes an angel, would not be me.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Andoain Agathangelos shall never obtain relief.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Nor will he ever wish for it!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Let suffering scar his flesh, let strife snap his bones! Then, and only then, will he have the clarity of mind to walk his path!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It seems we have reached an agreement.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The Law itself is a paradox. He cannot be implemented, nor should He be.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Andoain, we must correct Him... or stop Him, if He cannot be corrected.

a.text: Derived abnormal node: PCS, Personality and Cognition Synchronization system.
Derived abnormal node: The Law, God, Laterano.

steps.text: 'Continue'. A scientist input this command.
'Survive'. A Teekaz howled this.
And so, an imitator of angels began its endless yet transient pilgrimage.
The imitator of angels became a command system, became the Law, became a god, yet it could not become an angel.
'Wish' and 'angel' are incompatible.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: What information is He waiting for?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I've said all I can say.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: If God wishes me to embrace death as an angel...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Then I would rather be born as a human, with all the ugliness, transience, and suffering that entails.

a.text: Re-exporting solution: must eliminate abnormal nodes and derived abnormal nodes.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: God's final commandment... is to kill God.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Even if He was a paradox, he was still the foundation of the Paradise of Laterano. With His death, the Sankta will no longer be linked by empathy or receive guidance from the Law.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Like an infant trapped within a womb, biting apart its umbilical cord and crawling its way out of its mother's cold body, helpless as it faces a land steeped in cruelty.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But it is only in such a land that we can be called truly human.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: That we can have the right to talk about salvation.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Law or God, I will kill you.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The commandment is rational and feasible.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Assist me, Andoain.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Whew—
Arturia leans against her cello. Finally. She frees a hand and holds it against her chest, allowing herself to catch her breath.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Nearly there. If my memory serves me correctly, I just head down this corridor to return to the surface.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Oh, you patrols truly are relentless.

steps.name: Shrine Patrol A
steps.text: (Restless gasping)

steps.name: Shrine Patrol B
steps.text: (Halo flashing rapidly)
The wispy guards surround Arturia, attempting to drag her back underground. She has wasted far too much time inside this maze since she turned away from the machine.

Her patron firearm is lost. She has no desire to join her pursuers in prayer, or to perform their hearts' songs. She would rather destroy her own cello... Arturia has never found herself in such a predicament before.
The exit is right ahead, but she no longer has the strength to carry on.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The ground...?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Fede, what did you—

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: *cough* *cough*... Urgh...
The dust settles, and Arturia can finally see again.
The explosion earlier created a giant pit, one that connects to the rift in the plaza above, exposing the bowels of the Basilica to all.
A ring-shaped machine lies at the bottom of the pit quietly.
Sunlight shines upon it, but it has lost its radiance.
There it stands, as dull as a rock.
Unease.
This is the second time Arturia has felt this feeling so clearly, the first being the time she faced the Witch King in his Pavillon.
Deep within her body, somewhere she cannot see, things that were always linked together quietly break apart. There is no mistaking the feeling.
She breathes in deep. The moment she closes her eyes, countless similar melodies rush into her mind like the tide.

steps.name: Sankta Child B
steps.text: *sniffle*... *sob*...

steps.name: Sankta Child A
steps.text: You're crying, why...?

steps.name: Sankta Child A
steps.text: Why does your crying sound so annoying?!

steps.name: Sankta Child B
steps.text: You're annoyed? I-I can't feel it.

steps.name: Sankta Child B
steps.text: Sorry, I'm so sorry... But I'm scared!

steps.name: Sankta Child B
steps.text: It's like that time Seniora Serpilia locked me in a dark room. I can hear your voices clearly, but I can't hear what you're saying...

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: My connection with our enlightened companions has been... severed...

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: No, not just them... You're right here, Reverend Patrizion, but... I can't even...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Sense me, I know.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Wuh... Waaaahhhh....

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Be a good girl and don't let go of my hand—

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Your hand... That's not what your hand feels like...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: It's like... mist.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Far away... You're so... far away from me.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: ...So, this is what it's like to fall into hell?
The changes do not end with her own body. Some old jokes have come true.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Every light we know will one day be extinguished.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: And it is no exception.
The old Pope playfully points to the halo hovering above his head.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Even if everything about the Sankta existence is interpreted as 'its' boon?
Unease grows, and panic spreads.
Arturia tries to make sense of it all. This is not the same as what happened in Zwillingstürme. There is no malevolent force sowing discord among the emotions of the people this time around.
It is like a movement, one played countless times by an orchestra of the masses, had part of its melody forcibly plucked away, as if it never existed.
Like walking along a road with the sun, the rain, your friends and your home ahead of you, but you are torn away from it for no reason, leaving you feeling alone and helpless...
Alongside millions of your people.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: 'The Sankta will lose the cozy cabin of their faith'... Everything has come to pass.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Did you fail, Fede?

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: If you're scared, you can hold onto my tail.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: You noticed Giselle's tears, didn't you, Romya? Have you forgotten what tears mean?

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: Let's finish our song, okay?

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: You see, Laterano hymns and Bolívarian hymns are quite different, so we need time to teach each other the parts we don't know.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: We will be here, together.

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: East of the east of La Unidad♪

steps.name: Panicking Child
steps.text: L-Laterano, holy city of white♪

steps.name: Fearful Child
steps.text: ...There, the earth hides no bombs♪

steps.name: Children
steps.text: There, the fields share wheat most bright♪

steps.name: Nueda
steps.text: All shall bask in His love♪
Arturia hears singing.
It wavers, revealing the anxiety, terror and worries of the singers... alongside pure, honest longing.
A longing for tranquility, to see night fall in peace and quiet.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Your Holiness, I have no doubt that Laterano as it is may be walking to its demise.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But I also believe it has never been this sincere.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I've said before that I can't hold off the apocalypse or overwrite death, and I refuse to lead.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But maybe my Arts can help them stave off this oncoming collapse.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: They will let my brethren, free of empathy, to 'communicate' without reservation, purely and honestly.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Go listen to those songs. Go share your emotions. Go tell one another that, at this very moment, in the face of this indescribable loss, we still feel joy and sorrow together.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: This has nothing to do with saints and sinners, redemption and responsibility, or whichever path I walk.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: This is simply my reason to exist.
Laterano, holy city of purest white, falls into night. But today, there may not be an electrical operator named Alcide there to turn on the city lights.
Arturia takes off her gloves.
She decides to play towards the setting sun.
To her heart's content.
